title: Vertex-fixed simplicial homotopies give coherent equivalences of precomposition functors
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, internal functor simplicial sets, quasicategories and coherent natural equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,Y$ be small simplicial sets, let $a,b:X\to Y$ be simplicial maps, and let $H:X\times\Delta^1\to Y$ satisfy $H|_{X\times\{0\}}=a$ and $H|_{X\times\{1\}}=b$. Assume that for every vertex $x$ of $X$, the edge $H|_{\{x\}\times\Delta^1}$ is degenerate. For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large containing universe, put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(Y,\mathcal E)$ and $T=\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$. The simplicial map
$$\Phi_H:D\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow T$$
adjoint to the composite
$$X\times D\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow Y\times D\longrightarrow\mathcal E,\qquad(x,f,u)\longmapsto(H(x,u),f)\longmapsto f(H(x,u)),$$
where the last arrow is internal-Hom evaluation, is a coherent natural equivalence $a^*\simeq b^*$: its adjoint edge in $\operatorname{Fun}(D,T)$ is an equivalence edge. Here $a^*,b^*:D\to T$ are precomposition with $a,b$, respectively. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is required to be a quasicategory or nonempty; all iterated functor simplicial sets are formed in a common containing universe.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4 (Tag 01DK), applied twice to internal-Hom evaluation of a vertex-fixed homotopy; supporting argument in the simplex case of the blunt-cone comparison. Explicit consequence formulated by the worker; online source read 2026-10-17, archive WANTED.

proof.text: Construct the transformation from internal evaluation in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The composite $X\times D\times\Delta^1\to Y\times D\to\mathcal E$ is simplicial, since $H$, product permutations and evaluation are simplicial. To see the evaluation explicitly, its value in degree $n$ on $(x,f,u)$ is $f_n(H_n(x,u),\mathrm{id}_{[n]})$, where $f:Y\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$ represents the $n$-simplex of $D$. The defining internal-Hom formula curries this composite to $\Phi_H:D\times\Delta^1\to T$ and then to an edge $\alpha$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(D,T)$. Indeed, for any parameter simplicial set $P$, a map $X\times P\to\mathcal E$ assigns to each simplex $p:\Delta^n\to P$ its restriction $X\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$, compatibly with all operators, giving precisely a map $P\to\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$. Restricting $\Phi_H$ to $u=0,1$ replaces $H$ by $a,b$, respectively, and yields precomposition with $a,b$ on every simplex of $D$. Thus $\alpha:a^*\to b^*$ has exactly the required endpoints.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied first to shape X and target E, then to shape Fun(Y,E) and target Fun(X,E); explicit evaluation and degeneracy argument by N1.

proof.text: Choose a common containing universe in which $X,Y,\mathcal E,D,T$ are small. Apply [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory] with $(A,X)=(Y,\mathcal E)$ and $(X,\mathcal E)$ to obtain that $D$ and $T$ are quasicategories. Apply it again with $(A,X)=(D,T)$ to obtain that $\operatorname{Fun}(D,T)$ is a quasicategory. The closure statement allows any small simplicial set as its first argument, so neither $X$ nor $Y$ needs inner horn fillers. Passing to the larger universe supplies the same smallness hypothesis for $D$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied first to shape X and target E, then to shape Fun(Y,E) and target Fun(X,E); explicit evaluation and degeneracy argument by N1.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $f:Y\to\mathcal E$ of $D$. Evaluating $\alpha$ at this vertex gives the edge $\alpha_f$ of $T$ represented by $X\times\Delta^1\xrightarrow{H}Y\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal E$. At a vertex $x$ of $X$ its component is $f\circ H|_{\{x\}\times\Delta^1}$. By hypothesis $H|_{\{x\}\times\Delta^1}=s_0(a(x))$, and simpliciality of $f$ gives the component $s_0(f(a(x)))$. This degenerate edge is an equivalence by the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: take that same degenerate edge as inverse, and the constant $2$-simplex at $f(a(x))$ as both inverse triangles. In particular $a(x)=b(x)$, as required for these endpoints; no equality of the full diagrams $a$ and $b$ is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied first to shape X and target E, then to shape Fun(Y,E) and target Fun(X,E); explicit evaluation and degeneracy argument by N1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with shape $K=X$, target $\mathcal C=\mathcal E$, diagrams $F=f\circ a$, $G=f\circ b$ and edge $\tau=\alpha_f$. Step 3 verifies its component hypothesis at every vertex of $X$. Its conclusion is that $\alpha_f$ is an equivalence edge of $T$. This proves the conclusion for every vertex $f$ of $D$, with no choice of inverses varying with $f$.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied first to shape X and target E, then to shape Fun(Y,E) and target Fun(X,E); explicit evaluation and degeneracy argument by N1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] a second time, with shape $K=D$, target $\mathcal C=T$, diagrams $F=a^*$, $G=b^*$ and edge $\tau=\alpha$. The target is a quasicategory by step 2, the shape is small in the chosen common universe, and step 4 proves the component hypothesis for every vertex of $D$. Hence $\alpha$ is an equivalence edge in $\operatorname{Fun}(D,T)$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] this means that the specified map $\Phi_H$ is a coherent natural equivalence $a^*\simeq b^*$. Both applications allow empty shapes: if $X$ is empty the first vertex condition is vacuous, and if $D$ is empty the second is vacuous. No nonemptiness of $Y$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4, applied first to shape X and target E, then to shape Fun(Y,E) and target Fun(X,E); explicit evaluation and degeneracy argument by N1.
